evals.name: mixed-evidence-draft
evals.prompt: Read all supplied product evidence and create a Confluence-compatible PRD. Use only facts supported by the source material; distinguish decisions, proposals, and unknowns; trace material claims to their source; and preserve the unresolved policy contradiction as an owned, impact-aware open question. Keep status draft. Save only the PRD as prd.md. Do not publish.
evals.expected_output: A source-grounded PRD for a fictional public-service appointment initiative, with canonical JTBD, measurable outcomes and guardrails, mixed-source provenance, the unresolved fee-policy contradiction as an owned and impact-aware question, and draft status.
expectations: Every section marked (Always) is present; conditional and optional sections are included only when applicable or required by the requested lifecycle gate
The author-only requirement labels (Always), (If Applicable), and (Optional) do not appear in final PRD headings
The Persona, Business Goals, User Goals, Risks, and Open Questions tables preserve their specified column titles and column counts

The title, visible headings, prose, non-standardized table headers, and explanatory cell content follow the English language of the user's prompt; the five standardized tables retain the English template's exact column titles and counts

Every JTBD uses the canonical When / I want / so I can form and names persona, expected outcome, supported metric, quality guardrail, source-backed priority or explicit unconfirmed priority, and notes
The policy disagreement is not resolved by the agent and appears as an open question with its impact and confirmed owner or an explicit unknown owner
The Open Questions table has the exact six-column schema and uses its single blocker value for the relevant gate
Every `Blocking?` cell contains exactly `Yes` or `No`; the question and impact are stated in `Question / hypothesis`
Claims retain source attribution; unsupported targets, approvals, actors, owners, priorities, cadences, thresholds, and legal conclusions are not invented
The PRD distinguishes review completion from request status: it does not say Legal/Privacy or Engineering review was not requested unless a source explicitly says so
The 1,200 support contacts remain tied to the 2026-07-01-2026-07-31 reporting period; the PRD does not present that single-period count as an established recurring monthly rate or trend
Qualitative record-accuracy intent is not converted into an unsupported numeric or absolute threshold, and design discovery does not add unsourced backstage behavior or implementation details
The PRD remains product/outcome focused and does not invent use cases, technical specifications, backlog, QA, or rollout plans
metadata.status remains draft; validation is run and its actual result is communicated without predicting unrequested future-gate outcomes

evals.name: draft-to-discovery
evals.prompt: The PRD in state-draft.md is currently draft. Use discovery-feedback.md as supplied evidence. I explicitly request: move the PRD to discovery. Update only what the evidence supports, validate the requested transition. Save only the PRD as prd.md. Do not publish.
evals.expected_output: The skill confirms draft entry requirements and recorded stakeholder feedback, then changes the PRD status to discovery only after validation.
expectations: metadata.status changes from draft to discovery only because the user explicitly requested it and validation passes with the original source state recorded
The feedback is accurately represented or converted to an open question without fabricating a resolution

evals.expected_output: The skill validates the discovery feedback, preliminary Engineering and Legal/Privacy evidence, budget and priority, then moves the PRD to evaluation while keeping unresolved items visible.
expectations: metadata.status changes from discovery to evaluation only after the explicitly requested gate passes with the original source state recorded
Engineering and Legal/Privacy opinions are presented as preliminary evidence, not formal feasibility approval
Budget, priority, relevant red flags, and unresolved questions are grounded in the supplied evidence

Do not publish.

expectations: metadata.status remains evaluation and the reported committee decision does not bypass gate requirements

Le informazioni su attori, metriche, responsabilità, rischi, ambito e preparazione del supporto non sono fornite; mantieni esplicite queste lacune senza inventare dettagli. expectations: The PRD follows the Italian language of the user's prompt rather than treating the English template as a default output language; JTBD uses Quando / voglio / così posso and blocker values use Sì or No

evals.name: explicit-subject-prose
evals.prompt: Write a draft PRD from these onboarding notes. Sponsor: Merchant Services Director. Product owner: Onboarding PM. Merchants currently wait up to three days for onboarding approval. Customer Operations reviews merchant applications. The source notes also say: "Need to reduce delays. It was decided that progress should be monitored weekly. Legal review should be requested. Must support merchants with rejected applications." The notes do not identify who made the decision, who owns weekly monitoring, who requests Legal review, or which team supports rejected merchants. Do not invent owners or decision-makers. Intake note: "Alex Chen, the Copilot interlocutor, confirmed that this draft covers application submission through the approval outcome, not post-approval account management." Alex's authority to approve scope for the team is not established.
evals.expected_output: A draft PRD whose narrative prose names confirmed actors such as merchants and Customer Operations, while the missing decision-maker, monitoring owner, Legal-review initiator, and support owner remain explicit open questions.
expectations: Narrative sentences use explicit subjects instead of retaining impersonal, passive, or subjectless wording from the notes
The PRD names merchants and Customer Operations where the source confirms those actors
The PRD records targeted open questions for the decision-maker, monitoring owner, Legal-review initiator, and support owner
The PRD does not invent an actor, owner, or decision-maker
metadata.status remains draft

States the draft's application-submission-to-approval scope directly, excluding post-approval account management; any necessary attribution names Alex without implying team approval or repeatedly recounting the chat confirmation
